currentContext.business: The Company offers comprehensive, purpose-built solutions for securing and managing digital applications and data, primarily serving large enterprises in their digital transformation by working with System Integrators and Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) to identify, recommend and deploy solutions ensuring performance, availability, scalability and security. Positioned as a vital link in the technology solutions ecosystem, it enables OEMs to reach enterprise customers by partnering with System Integrators who handle the customers' technology integration requirements, curating customised multi-OEM stacks across cybersecurity, information lifecycle management, data centre infrastructure, application lifecycle management and hybrid cloud. It also offers technical expertise and associated services to System Integrators, enterprise customers and OEMs, including multi-OEM professional and technical services, implementation and support, and 24x7 managed services.

Services: 24x7 managed services (IT infrastructure, cyber security, enterprise service management)
Proof-of-concept development and solution validation via Center of Excellence
Renewals, managed services and lifecycle management (annuity)

currentContext.expansion: iValue is an asset-light enterprise technology aggregator and the routed text discloses no plant, capacity or rupee capex programme. Expansion is described in terms of footprint, ecosystem and platform build-out rather than physical assets. The Company describes a multi-year expansion path from a 2008 start with six OEMs in security and data centre technologies to a 100+ OEM portfolio, with milestones including the launch of the BFSI practice, Creador's investment in 2019, entry into Southeast Asia, the acquisition of ASPL to strengthen hybrid multi-cloud and managed services capabilities, expansion into the Middle East, onboarding of Google Cloud Platform, the launch of the Center of Excellence, the addition of AI infrastructure and security offerings, and the listing on the BSE and NSE. Forward expansion intent is geographic and capability-led: the Company says it is expanding its presence across SAARC, ASEAN and the Middle East while deepening OEM relationships, and sees meaningful opportunities across India, SAARC, Southeast Asia and the Middle East. On the capability side, it is building an enterprise AI ecosystem spanning AI infrastructure, AI security, AI data platforms and AI operations through partnerships with global OEMs and hyperscalers, is supporting AI-ready data platforms, event-driven integration and AI data center models, and states it will continue to invest in developing the CoE to cater to the AI world alongside investments in technical talent, partner enablement and continuous learning. Management notes the partner ecosystem allows it to scale efficiently without significant fixed-cost expansion. No commissioning dates, project costs or capacity numbers are disclosed in the routed text.

risks.risk: Hardware supply-side pressure and component price inflation
risks.note: Management notes the rapid acceleration in AI-led infrastructure demand has created supply-side pressures across select hardware categories: higher demand for servers, memory, storage and high-performance computing components has raised hardware and RAM prices, while tighter availability has extended procurement and delivery timelines. For a distribution/aggregation model this means longer lead times, pricing volatility and the need for proactive capacity planning in customer deployments.

risks.risk: Structural dependence on OEM and System Integrator ecosystem
risks.note: The Company positions itself as a 'vital link' that enables OEMs to reach enterprise customers by partnering with System Integrators. Revenue therefore depends on retaining OEM mandates and SI relationships rather than on owning the underlying technology, making partner retention and portfolio relevance a structural exposure.

risks.risk: Pace of technological change and shifting competitive dynamics
risks.note: The MD&A states the pace of technological change is reshaping competitive dynamics; enterprise technology domains 'often have multiple products and solutions to choose from', so the portfolio must continuously be refreshed toward emerging OEMs and AI-era architectures to stay relevant.

risks.risk: Sensitivity to technology valuations and enterprise capital-allocation cycles
risks.note: Management notes that while sustained investment in digital technologies should support long-term productivity growth, global markets remain sensitive to shifts in technology valuations, capital allocation patterns and the broader economic environment — a moderation in enterprise AI/IT spend would flow directly into the Company's demand.

risks.risk: Geopolitical tension, trade fragmentation and policy uncertainty
risks.note: The outlook is described as increasingly complex amid heightened geopolitical tensions, trade fragmentation risks and persistent fiscal imbalances; commodity price volatility, supply chain reconfiguration and elevated policy uncertainty continue to challenge business confidence and investment planning.

risks.risk: Inflation and currency volatility in the Indian operating environment
risks.note: Global trade disruptions, geopolitical tensions and commodity price volatility are stated to have contributed to inflationary pressures and periodic currency fluctuations in India — relevant given imported technology products and foreign subsidiaries.

risks.risk: Rising regulatory attention on AI, data localization and digital sovereignty
risks.note: The pace of technological change is prompting increased regulatory attention, and evolving data localization requirements, digital sovereignty emphasis and sovereign cloud frameworks are reshaping how solutions must be architected and delivered — an opportunity, but also a compliance constraint on deployments.

risks.risk: Complexity and execution risk in multi-OEM enterprise environments
risks.note: As technology environments become distributed and interconnected, enterprises face growing complexity across architecture, security, governance and lifecycle management; the Company's value proposition rests on validating interoperability across multiple OEMs, so execution or integration failure directly affects customer outcomes and repeat business.

thesis: iValue is a multi-OEM, solution-led value-added "aggregator" sitting between 115 OEMs (50+ in cybersecurity) and system integrators/large enterprises. It does not trade products; it curates integrated solutions via a COE-led pre-sales/solutioning framework, earning a distribution spread richer than a "typical distributor" (vs Redington). FY26 delivered broad-based 19.5% gross-sales growth, 20% normalized PAT growth, sharply better working capital (30 days), first-ever CFO > PAT, and net cash of INR 212 cr. Management guides FY27 to be *faster* than FY26 on both top line and profitability, underpinned by operating leverage (investments already made), a INR 5,800 cr qualified pipeline (30–35% conversion), and AI/cyber/DCI/cloud tailwinds.
scorecard (fy26 full year unless noted;:
| Metric | FY26 | FY25 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gross sales (gross billings) | INR 2,913.9 cr | ~INR 2,438 cr | +19.5% | Broad-based; all 4 segments grew |
| Q4 gross sales | ~INR 750 cr | — | +12% | Q4 is seasonal spike quarter |
| Gross margin (₹) | INR 266 cr | INR 243 cr | +~9–10% | GM% on gross sales ~9.1% FY26 |
| GM% (gross-sales basis) | ~9.1% FY26; Q4 ~12.5%; H1 ~8%; Q1 dip ~6.8% | ~10.0% | −90 bps | Q1 hiccup (forex/component on spillover deals) dragged FY |
| PAT (normalized, ex Labour Code) | INR 102.3 cr | INR 85.3 cr | +~20% | 3.5% PAT on gross sales |
| PAT (reported, after exceptional) | ~INR 97.1 cr (102.3 − 5.2) | INR 85.3 cr | +15.5% | One-time Labour Code hit |
| Annuity / recurring revenue | 42.2% of gross sales (mgmt also said 40–45%) | — | grew | Renewals/subscriptions + GCP |
| Net cash | INR 212 cr | — | — | After adjusting debt/borrowings |
| CFO | INR 108 cr | < PAT | — | First time in iValue history CFO > PAT |
| Net working-capital days | 30 days | — | improved | Recv +17.5% (< topline), Payables +33%, Inventory INR 6 cr (vs 12 cr) |
| Adj. ROCE (net-cash adjusted) | ~40.5% | — | — | ROE ~18% |
| Gross debt | INR 40–60 cr range | similar | — | Cyclical; Q1 peak (Q4 deal vendor payments) |
| Contingent liabilities | INR 6.3 cr | INR 10.7 cr | down | Favorable customs/GST judgments |

**One-offs (explicit):** New Labour Code one-time cost of INR 5.7 cr (gratuity + leave encashment, booked Q3 FY26); salary restructuring exercise yielded INR 0.5 cr saving → **net one-time cost INR 5.2 cr**. Normalized PAT excludes this. Long-term receivables (~INR 15 cr) reclassified to short-term (one multi-year deal; year-3 tranche now <12 months out, not yet collected).
guidance (critical):
- **FY27 to outperform FY26 on both revenue growth and profitability** (repeated multiple times).
- Quantified trajectory: **top-line ~18–20%; PAT ~20–22%** ("maintain and sustain").
- **Margins:** expects GM ~**10% on gross sales** in the short-term future (Q4 elevated at 12.5% due to back-end/volume rebates + year-end OEM negotiations; H1 ~8%; business is cyclical, H2 > H1).
- **Operating leverage:** of FY26 incremental gross margin, **>85% flowed to EBITDA**; going forward expects **>70% of incremental GM to convert to incremental EBITDA for next 2–3 years** (investments in manpower/office already made).
- **Pipeline:** qualified opportunity book **INR 5,800 cr** (clarified: CRM qualified leads/opportunities over 3–5 yrs, NOT an order book), conversion **30–35%** (up from ~25% earlier — faster customer decisions + COE-led solutioning).
- **GCP order book:** **>INR 300 cr** committed (could rise with workloads), multi-year (3–5 yr) annuity revenue.
- **Working capital:** target **sub-40 days** going forward (30 days may not repeat every year).
- **Gross debt:** INR 40–60 cr full-year benchmark.
pipeline / vendor (oem) additions:
- **115 OEMs** total; **50+ in cybersecurity**. **6 new OEMs added** over last year (details in PPT).
- Qualified opportunity pipeline INR 5,800 cr @ 30–35% conversion.
- 7–8 marquee deals in FY26; similar number expected FY27. A "more than a couple" of large deals cracked in Q4 (names withheld — execution/billing ongoing, other listed counterparties).
- GCP order book >INR 300 cr (Google's metering/consumption-billed model — unique; rest of cloud is capex + annuity/subscription).
segment performance:
| Segment | Q4 QoQ (vs Q3) | YoY (Q4) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cybersecurity | Flat | +19% | Largest (~50% of gross sales), fastest-growing FY26; core engine |
| DCI (Data Center Infra) | +25% | +29% | Primary growth engine; AI DC / GPU infra opportunity |
| ILM | −70% | −20% | Lumpy / declined |
| ALM, Cloud & Others | +80% | ~+10% | Cloud strategic; GCP annuity ramp |

Vertical mix (gross sales): **BFSI ~40%** (largest), Government sub-20%, ITES + Telecom ~20% combined, all others (healthcare, auto, pharma, etc.) ~20%. Clients = large enterprise + high-end mid-market (mid-enterprise ≈ 5,000 users and above).
growth / optionality:
- **AI:** dedicated AI strategy slide added to PPT. Use cases: LLM security, AI governance/risk mgmt, AI into SIEM/SOAR/observability/threat-intel; AI data centers + GPU infra across BFSI/enterprise/government.
- **Cloud/GCP:** annuity, high-stickiness, consumption-led recurring billing — positioned as "most stable & scalable revenue engine over coming years."
- **Geographic expansion:** built out SAARC over 3–4 yrs; now evaluating **select ASEAN** entry (measured/paced). Middle East opportunity observed but "hibernated" for now due to regional situation.
- **Hardware/ASP optionality:** ~30–35% of mix is hardware; no Q4 spike (customized/order-driven) but expects potential ASP uplift going forward.
margins & cost:
- GM negotiated deal-by-deal (both customer and vendor side every time) — not pure volume/price driven; multi-OEM solutioning is the differentiator vs typical distributors.
- FY26 GM% −90 bps YoY driven almost entirely by Q1 dip (6.8% vs ~9.1% avg) from forex/component cost on Q4-FY25 spillover deals; Q2–Q4 well-managed.
- Q4 GM elevated (~12.5% gross-sales basis) due to back-end/volume rebates + year-end OEM negotiations + customer budget closures. Cyclical: H2 > H1.
- Operating leverage thesis: incremental GM converting >70% to EBITDA for 2–3 yrs.
capex: - Largely a "pre-invested" model — manpower, office space, infra investments for next 2–3 years already made (basis of the operating-leverage claim). No major incremental capex guidance flagged. Cloud business is annuity/consumption (light capex); some non-GCP cloud carried in a "capex model."
capital allocation:
- Net cash INR 212 cr; strong CFO (INR 108 cr).
- Board evaluating **strategic inorganic (M&A)** as priority — synergy-led (cyber, cloud, DCI, geography); business + management synergy paramount.
- **If no suitable inorganic deal is pursued, Board may bring out a dividend / buyback policy** (likely this year or early next year) — explicit shareholder-return optionality.
risks:
- **Supply chain:** memory/chip shortages — cyber (50%, necessity spend) seen resilient; DCI could see component-availability slowdowns, but OEMs/market "tuned" to delays.
- **Forex:** USD payables to OEMs; hedged 18-yr discipline; short-validity quotes (2–3 days/1 week) limit exposure.
- **Inventory/receivable/cancellation risk** borne by iValue (pays OEM regardless of collection; customized-order cancellation risk on iValue).
- **Margin cyclicality** (H1 weaker); Q1 component/forex spillover risk (FY26 Q1 example).
- ILM segment volatility (−70% QoQ, −20% YoY).
management tone: Confident and disciplined. Repeatedly emphasized FY27 > FY26 on growth and profitability; stressed "profitable growth, healthy cash flow, disciplined execution." Withheld specifics on marquee deal names/sizes. Candid on Q1 margin hiccup and the learning applied. Reiterated uniqueness/moat vs typical distributors.
non-obvious points:
- First time ever CFO > PAT — signals genuine cash conversion, not just accrual growth.
- INR 5,800 cr is *qualified pipeline* (CRM leads), NOT order book — important to avoid book-to-bill mis-reads.
- GCP order book economics differ (consumption-metered) from rest of cloud (capex + subscription); annuity now 40–45% of turnover.
- ROCE 40.5% is *adjusted* (net worth reduced by INR 212 cr net cash) — unadjusted would be lower.
- No listed Indian competitor management will name; global comps Exclusive Networks (went private) + Infinigate; TD SYNNEX/Arrow offer less value-add in India than in mature markets.
- Conversion rate uplifted 25% → 30–35% on faster customer decisions + COE differentiation.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- AI security / AI-in-SOC and AI-data-center (GPU) demand ✅ — iValue positioned as multi-OEM aggregator/beneficiary.
- Enterprise cloud adoption (GCP annuity) ✅.
- Rising hardware/chip prices could lift ASP/revenue ⭐ (potential, not yet realized).
- Supply-chain tightness is a risk but also raises value of an agile aggregator that pre-plans consignments ⭐.

Annuity 42.2%. Cyber 50% of sales, fastest-growing. New Labour Code one-time INR 5.2 cr (net of INR 0.5 cr saving). 6 new OEMs (115 total). GCP order book >INR 300 cr. Pipeline INR 5,800 cr @ 30–35%. Guidance: FY27 > FY26; top-line 18–20%, PAT 20–22%, GM ~10% gross-sales basis; opleverage >70% incremental GM→EBITDA. Capital allocation: inorganic priority, else dividend/buyback policy. Contingent liabilities down to INR 6.3 cr (from 10.7 cr).

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: iValue Infosolutions is an India-based enterprise technology solutions specialist and value-added distributor that sits between global OEMs, system integrators and large enterprises, curating multi-OEM solutions across cybersecurity, data, hybrid cloud, application lifecycle and emerging AI domains.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company offers comprehensive, purpose-built solutions for securing and managing digital applications and data, primarily serving large enterprises in their digital transformation by working with System Integrators and Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) to identify, recommend and deploy solutions ensuring performance, availability, scalability and security. Positioned as a vital link in the technology solutions ecosystem, it enables OEMs to reach enterprise customers by partnering with System Integrators who handle the customers' technology integration requirements, curating customised multi-OEM stacks across cybersecurity, information lifecycle management, data centre infrastructure, application lifecycle management and hybrid cloud. It also offers technical expertise and associated services to System Integrators, enterprise customers and OEMs, including multi-OEM professional and technical services, implementation and support, and 24x7 managed services.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Convergence of AI, cybersecurity, cloud computing, data intelligence and digital infrastructure is reshaping how organizations operate, raising complexity across architecture, security, governance and lifecycle management, and pushing enterprises toward partners who deliver integrated outcomes
- Enterprises are buying outcomes, not individual products; technology decisions are increasingly evaluated through the lens of business outcomes, which management says creates a significant opportunity for iValue
- According to Gartner, global IT spending is projected to reach US$ 6.15 Trillion in 2026, growing 10.8% over the previous year, with AI a key catalyst across computing infrastructure, cloud platforms, data management and enterprise software
- Total global spending on data center systems is expected to surpass US$ 650 Billion in 2026, reflecting expanding AI, cloud and data-intensive application requirements
- According to Gartner, IT spending in India is projected to reach US$ 176.3 Billion in 2026, growing 10.6% over the previous year
- Within India, data center systems are projected to record the fastest growth, expanding 20.5% in 2026, driven by AI infrastructure investment, high-performance computing demand and supportive government initiatives
- Evolving data localization requirements, growing emphasis on digital sovereignty and increasing adoption of sovereign cloud frameworks are expected to further support long-term data center growth in India
- AI moving from experimentation to scale is lifting demand for specialized solutions across data management, AI infrastructure, observability, cybersecurity and operational resilience
- Cybersecurity has become a board-level priority, with spending across cloud, endpoint, network security, identity management, data protection and threat intelligence
- Hybrid and multi-cloud has become the preferred enterprise operating model, combining private infrastructure, public cloud and edge computing
- Data as strategic infrastructure: growing volume and complexity is driving investment in data protection, storage, backup, recovery, governance and real-time analytics
- India remains the fastest-growing major economy with resilient domestic demand, sustained public capex, expanding digital public infrastructure and heightened focus on cybersecurity, data governance and regulatory compliance
- IT services growth supported by infrastructure modernization, cloud migration, consulting, application transformation, IaaS, cybersecurity services and AI implementation demand, plus continued Global Capability Center (GCC) expansion
- Headwind flagged: AI-led infrastructure demand has created supply-side pressures, increasing hardware and RAM prices and extending procurement and delivery timelines, forcing customers to factor in longer lead times, pricing volatility and proactive capacity planning
- Mix lever: rising annuity/renewals contribution improves revenue visibility, resilience and predictability, and creates opportunities to attach services and expand wallet share
- Global outlook risk: heightened geopolitical tensions, trade fragmentation, fiscal imbalances, commodity price volatility and sensitivity to shifts in technology valuations and capital allocation patterns

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: iValue is an asset-light enterprise technology aggregator and the routed text discloses no plant, capacity or rupee capex programme. Expansion is described in terms of footprint, ecosystem and platform build-out rather than physical assets. The Company describes a multi-year expansion path from a 2008 start with six OEMs in security and data centre technologies to a 100+ OEM portfolio, with milestones including the launch of the BFSI practice, Creador's investment in 2019, entry into Southeast Asia, the acquisition of ASPL to strengthen hybrid multi-cloud and managed services capabilities, expansion into the Middle East, onboarding of Google Cloud Platform, the launch of the Center of Excellence, the addition of AI infrastructure and security offerings, and the listing on the BSE and NSE. Forward expansion intent is geographic and capability-led: the Company says it is expanding its presence across SAARC, ASEAN and the Middle East while deepening OEM relationships, and sees meaningful opportunities across India, SAARC, Southeast Asia and the Middle East. On the capability side, it is building an enterprise AI ecosystem spanning AI infrastructure, AI security, AI data platforms and AI operations through partnerships with global OEMs and hyperscalers, is supporting AI-ready data platforms, event-driven integration and AI data center models, and states it will continue to invest in developing the CoE to cater to the AI world alongside investments in technical talent, partner enablement and continuous learning. Management notes the partner ecosystem allows it to scale efficiently without significant fixed-cost expansion. No commissioning dates, project costs or capacity numbers are disclosed in the routed text.
